To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exact filter for the state of the doubly stochastic AR model with conditionally Poissons observations is the conditional expectation of the state with respect to the sufficient statistic, that the sufficient statistic can be computed by solving a set of linear differential equations, that the sufficient statistics can be computed recursively, and that the exact filter can be computed recursively.

(a) the exact filter can be expressed in terms of an expectation with respect to the conditional distribution of the Gauss-Marcov process given the observed data; (b) this distribution can be obtained from the conditional distribution of a Gaussian random vector; (c) the conditional distribution of this Gaussian vector can be obtained from its marginal distribution, the conditional distribution of an exponential random variable, the conditional distribution and the conditional expectation of the number of Poisson events in an exponential random variable; and

1) the exact filter for the AR state is a linear combination of a finite number of conditional expectations of the Gauss-Marcov process and 2) the sufficient statistic for the exact filter is the number of observations.
